 India-Made Toothpaste Recalls Topped 4 Million Units Twice in Under 18 Months as Kids' Brands Join the List
 Published Oct 24, 2026 10:27 PM EDT 
 By
 Dorothy Brooks 
 Editorial Illustration via AI 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 The 4.3 million-tube toothpaste recall now reaching families is at least the second recall of toothpaste made by an Indian manufacturer to top 4 million units in less than 18 months. In spring 2025, the FDA posted an update on a recall of 4,617,316 toothpaste tubes and sachets from Kenil Healthcare Private Limited of India, also for deviations from current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) rules, The Healthy reported . Those products were distributed in Delaware and North Carolina by a company that supplies correctional facilities. Both recalls cited the same broad reason and gave the public few details about what went wrong.
 For parents, the concern is not an immediate poisoning risk. No illnesses or injuries have been reported, and the FDA rated the current recall Class II. The deeper issue is that fluoride toothpaste is an over-the-counter drug that children use twice a day, and families often learn about quality problems only through federal databases that most shoppers do not monitor.
 The current recall appeared in the FDA's weekly enforcement report listing the recalled toothpaste products . That matters when the products carry Barbie, Hot Wheels, and Crayola designs aimed at young children.
 A Pattern in Overseas Toothpaste Manufacturing
 MedicalDaily previously reported on the brands, flavors, and lot checks in the Brush Buddies recall . That coverage helped families find affected tubes. This report focuses on a different question: how often imported toothpaste falls short of federal manufacturing rules, and how much the public is told when it does.
 The FDA has taken stronger action against at least one other Indian toothpaste maker. In 2023, it sent a warning letter to Daxal Cosmetics Private Limited , a firm registered as a maker of over-the-counter drugs, including toothpaste, after the company failed to respond to FDA requests for records. The agency had already placed all of the firm's drug products on an import alert, which allows shipments to be detained at the border.
 These past actions do not show that the current toothpaste is contaminated. The enforcement report cites only CGMP deviations, and the FDA has not said whether testing found a defect in the product itself. In its explanation of manufacturing quality rules , the FDA says a drug made in violation of CGMP does not necessarily have something wrong with it.
 Key Facts in the Pritam International Recall
 Pritam International Private Limited, an India-based manufacturer, began the voluntary recall on Sept. 10, and the FDA classified it as Class II on Oct. 19. The recall covers 4,301,700 tubes across more than a dozen products sold under the Brush Buddies, evo, and ARU brands, including Brush Buddies toothpastes with Barbie, Hot Wheels, Crayola, and My Little Pony designs. Ashtel Studios Inc. of Ontario, California, distributed the products nationwide.
 Children's products make up a large share, including Barbie bubble gum (409,800 tubes), Hot Wheels strawberry (411,600 tubes), and three Crayola Silly Scents flavors (more than 960,000 tubes combined). But the single largest item is an adult product, Brush Buddies Whitening Anti-Cavity Fluoride Toothpaste with Baking Soda in Cool Mint, at nearly 798,000 tubes, according to Fox Business . Reported expiration dates run from November 2026 through June 2028, so families should match the exact lot number rather than rely on a date range.
 Manufacturing rules exist for a reason. The FDA says following them "assures the identity, strength, quality, and purity of drug products." A Class II rating means use of the product may cause temporary or medically reversible health effects, while the chance of serious harm is considered remote.
 Children, Caregivers, and Budget Shoppers Face the Most Exposure
 Young children are the group parents worry about most, because sweet flavors can encourage them to swallow toothpaste. Households that buy value packs or multi-tube bundles may have several affected tubes in different bathrooms.
 Adults are affected, too. Whitening, sensitivity, and gum-health pastes from evo, ARU, and Brush Buddies are on the list, so caregivers should check their own tubes, not only their children's.
 There is no evidence of a widespread health problem. Still, parents who notice mouth irritation, stomach upset, or other new symptoms after a child used a recalled tube should call a pediatrician or dentist. If a child swallows more than the amount used for brushing of any fluoride toothpaste, standard label directions say to get medical help or contact Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 right away. Trouble breathing, repeated vomiting, or unusual drowsiness warrants urgent care.
 Practical Steps for Families and What Comes Next
 Compare the lot number and expiration date on each tube or carton with the FDA enforcement report. If they match, stop using the product, photograph the label, and contact the retailer or manufacturer about a return or refund. Children should keep brushing with an unaffected fluoride toothpaste, because skipping fluoride raises the risk of cavities. There is no need to throw out every tube in the house.
 Families who want earlier warnings can check the FDA's weekly enforcement reports or sign up for recall alerts. Asking a pharmacist or dentist about trusted brands is also reasonable, especially for young children.
 Key questions remain unanswered. The FDA has not described the specific manufacturing failure or explained how the problem was discovered, and Fox Business reported that neither Pritam International nor the FDA could immediately be reached for comment.
 The recall is listed as ongoing. Any added lots, a stated cause, or further FDA action against the manufacturer would appear in future enforcement reports.

 Key Questions Answered
 Is this the first large toothpaste recall tied to an Indian manufacturer? No. In 2025, Kenil Healthcare of India recalled more than 4.6 million toothpaste tubes and sachets for manufacturing-practice deviations. The current recall from Pritam International covers about 4.3 million tubes.
 Where did the FDA announce the recall? The recall appears in the FDA's weekly enforcement report, which lists the affected products, lot numbers, and expiration dates.
 Is the recalled toothpaste dangerous? The FDA classified it as Class II, meaning any health effects are expected to be temporary or medically reversible. No illnesses have been reported.
 Are adult toothpastes included? Yes. The largest single product is Brush Buddies Whitening toothpaste with baking soda, and evo and ARU adult pastes are also listed.
 What should parents do if their child used a recalled tube? Stop using it and switch to an unaffected fluoride toothpaste. Call a pediatrician or dentist if new symptoms appear, and contact Poison Control if a child swallowed a large amount.
 Why was the toothpaste recalled? The FDA lists deviations from current good manufacturing practice rules. It has not described the specific problem.
